summary: Round 9, test-reviewer lane. Decomposition commit: no tests, so the question is whether each row obliges a test that would fail if the production code were wrong. Both round-8 items in my lane are discharged. The uncheckpointed tail now reads as a COST gap and I verified the three facts it rests on against the tree: SegmentCommit carries the rendered segment key (SegmentKey holds podShortId and a per-pod sequence), RunCommit carries firstOffset and recordCount so the original offsets are recoverable, and CommitDelta is (sequence, segments) with no flushSeq -- so 'only flushSeq is absent' is exact, and the substitution that makes it a cost gap holds: a retried flush carries the SAME segment key while a restarted pod reissuing flushSeq 0 carries a DIFFERENT one, which is the discriminator M4.10d needs. It agrees with M4.10b's third property, which forbids the backwards walk. The goldens claim is now true by deletion: format/src/test/resources/golden holds exactly one checkpoint golden, checkpoint-v0.bin. Three minors carried from round 8 remain, none of which must land here; one has become slightly more likely to bite and is noted as such. One further minor is recorded honestly as MY MISS at round 8 rather than as a new finding on unchanged text.

findings.claim: M4.10d says INVERT the tripwire but not RENAME it, and the row's wording now steers harder toward an assertion-line-only edit.
findings.failure_scenario: sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/CheckpointWriterContentTest.java:133 is named theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll and its body asserts doesNotContainKey("poda") at line 156. M4.10d's fold makes that name FALSE while the test still passes. The row's new sentence -- 'INVERT ... Deleting that assertion instead is the testing.md rule 5 inversion' -- pushes a session toward the minimal edit: flip line 156, leave line 133. The result is a green test whose name asserts the opposite of its body, violating testing.md rule 12, and a future reader navigating by name concludes the takeover still drops the pods map. This is not a surviving mutation in the production code -- the assertion itself is correctly inverted -- it is a durable false statement left in the suite, which is why it is minor and not major. It got MORE likely since round 8 because the row's language tightened around the assertion line.
findings.suggested_remedy: Two extra words in the row: 'invert AND RENAME'. Not worth a round on its own; fold into the next edit if one happens.

findings.claim: The rule-5 protection on the tripwire is prose, and the gate that would catch it scores the assertion at zero. Unchanged in force since round 8, and if anything now weaker in consequence.
findings.failure_scenario: Re-measured: scripts/test_integrity.py STRENGTH (lines 29-46) contains no doesNotContainKey pattern, so that assertion contributes 0. CheckpointWriterContentTest#theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll scores only from containsEntry("poda", 42L) at line 145, weight 2. A session that DELETES line 156 rather than inverting it leaves the method's strength at 2 -- unchanged -- so check-test-integrity.sh sees no weakening and the commit-msg gate passes. The only thing stopping the deletion is a sentence in a backlog row, which is rung 6/7 where rung 1 (one regex in the STRENGTH table) exists. WHAT CHANGED SINCE ROUND 8, in the row's favour: the tripwire is now explicitly the CORROBORATING half and the successor's refusal is the primary anchor, so losing the tripwire no longer costs the row its anchor. That lowers the cost of the gate's blindness rather than raising it.
findings.suggested_remedy: Add doesNotContainKey/doesNotContain/hasNoNullFieldsOrProperties to test_integrity.py's STRENGTH table -- a separate, mechanical, one-line change that belongs in its own commit and must not widen this one.

findings.claim: The fixture's co-landing obligation names M4.10, which will now never be a commit, and M4.10d's row does not name the fixture.
findings.failure_scenario: FakeSequencer's javadoc states that idempotency 'is M4.10's task and lands here in the same commit as the real behaviour so the two cannot drift'. After the split, the real behaviour lands in M4.10d, whose row lists FaultInjectingStore.Faults as the retry seam and never mentions the fake. If M4.10d lands the dedup without touching the fake, every T0 test built on FakeSequencer -- including IngestCommitPathTest, which at line 81-87 explicitly reasons about (podId, flushSeq) -- keeps exercising a fake that assigns fresh offsets to a replay while the real sequencer refuses it. That is precisely the drift the fixture's own javadoc exists to prevent, and no gate sees it. MITIGATION THAT KEEPS THIS MINOR: the obligation is written at the site that must change, which is stronger than a backlog row, and 'M4.10' still resolves -- backlog.md keeps the M4.10 banner marked split, the same convention M4.8 and M4.8b already use, so a reader following the reference is routed to b/c/d rather than stranded. Unchanged since round 8.
findings.suggested_remedy: None required here. When M4.10d is picked up, its first act is to re-point the fixture javadoc at M4.10d and land the fake's dedup in the same commit.

findings.claim: MY MISS AT ROUND 8, recorded rather than presented as new: M4.10b's commit-path-rate property is stated as an ADR obligation and no row obliges the failing test that would catch its violation.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.10b's third property forbids any commit-path request that scales with pod count, and names the exact violating shape (a per-pod ctl/pods/<podId> object rewritten every commit). M4.10b is an ADR row and produces prose. M4.10c is conditional and may be void. M4.10d enumerates what to assert -- refusal, original offsets, no delta appended, three surviving mutations -- and names no request-count assertion. So if b answers 'no format change', c voids, and d implements a per-pod PUT, every assertion any row names still passes while the commit-path PUT rate multiplies by the pod count: the exact regression M4.7 exists to prevent, invisible to the suite the decomposition specifies. The tree already has the idiom (RecordingBinStore plus the existing cost suites), so this is a gap in the row text, not in the harness. WHY THIS IS MINOR AND NOT MAJOR: testing.md rule 22 and cost.md's Enforcement section bind the implementing row independently of what the backlog says, so the assertion is doubly covered even unstated. AND THE TEXT DID NOT CHANGE THIS ROUND -- raising it now is me catching my own round-8 omission, not a defect the author introduced. Do not spend a round on it; this project's own M0.76 entry records what happens when each round's fix breeds the next round's finding.
findings.suggested_remedy: If M4.10d is edited for any other reason, add 'and a request-count assertion on the commit path'. Otherwise leave it -- rule 22 carries it.

answers_to_questions_posed.half_clause_rendering: CORRECT AND VERIFIED, and it is stronger than what I asked for. I asked only that the tail be distinguished as cost rather than information; the row now names both halves and closes the loop to M4.10b's cost property, so the two rows constrain each other instead of merely coexisting. I checked the three facts rather than accepting them: format/src/main/java/binjava/format/SegmentCommit.java:25 is (String segmentKey, List<RunCommit>), SegmentKey (format .../SegmentKey.java:39) renders prefix/timestampMillis/podShortId/sequence, RunCommit.java:19 is (RunKey, int recordCount, long firstOffset) and ChainReplay reads run.lastOffset(), and CommitDelta.java:28 is (long sequence, List<SegmentCommit>) with no flushSeq anywhere in the file. So 'only flushSeq is absent from the chain' is exact. The substitution that makes it a COST gap also holds under the row's own discriminator: a retried flush replays the SAME segment key (so the chain can answer it) while a restarted pod reissuing flushSeq 0 writes a DIFFERENT one (so it is correctly accepted). And the forbidden mechanism is named at the right place -- M4.10b's third property already calls a backwards walk 'the same fault in GETs'. Net effect on the suite M4.10d will write: it tells that session the information exists and only its retrieval cost is at issue, which rules out paying a per-commit PUT to duplicate what the chain already holds.
answers_to_questions_posed.length_prefix_absence: ITS ABSENCE DOES NOT WEAKEN THE PROPERTY, and I withdraw the suggestion rather than restate it. Two reasons, in the order that matters. FIRST, THE FAILURE DIRECTION IS SAFE: the property's obligation -- 'say what happens to a window recovered from a checkpoint written BEFORE the change' -- is unconditional, and the qualifying-the-String clause is there only to show the obligation survives an answer of 'no formats change'. If that clause were WRONG (if lengthening the pod key did change the format), the hazard would be larger and the obligation more obviously binding. An omitted citation whose falsity can only strengthen the requirement is not load-bearing. SECOND, IT IS VERIFIABLE AT THE LOCATION THE ROW ALREADY NAMES: the row says 'inside Checkpoint.pods's existing String', and Checkpoint.encode (format/src/main/java/binjava/format/Checkpoint.java:129-137) writes putUvarint(raw.length), the UTF-8 bytes, then putUvarint(flushSeq) -- a length-prefixed field, so a longer pod key shifts one uvarint and nothing structural. That took me under a minute from the pointer the row gives. Adding the reason alongside the correction is what generated the last five rounds here; do not add it.
answers_to_questions_posed.three_minors_still_hold: YES for all three, with one movement in each direction and neither changing the verdict. WORSE: the tripwire rename. The row's tightened 'INVERT ... deleting it is the rule 5 inversion' now steers toward editing line 156 alone and leaving the method name at line 133 asserting the opposite of its body. BETTER: the gate blindness. doesNotContainKey still scores 0, so a deletion is still invisible to check-test-integrity.sh, but the tripwire is now explicitly the corroborating half rather than the anchor, so the blindness costs less than it did at round 8. UNCHANGED: FakeSequencer's co-landing note, which is safe because the obligation sits at the site that must change and 'M4.10' still resolves to a split banner in backlog.md, the M4.8/M4.8b convention. None must land here; all three would widen a decomposition commit into a code commit.

what_i_verified_by_mutation: For a decomposition commit the mutation test is applied to the assertions the rows PRESCRIBE. Return-a-constant refusal (refuse everything) is killed by 'the restarted pod reissuing 0 for a NEW segment must be ACCEPTED'. Drop-the-side-effect is killed by 'assert no delta carrying the replayed segment key was appended', and the row correctly explains why the obvious assertion cannot do it: ChainReplay.java:441 folds with merge(key, lastOffset + 1, Math::max), so re-appending at the original absolute offsets leaves nextOffset unchanged and an offsets assertion is structurally blind. Boundary flip is killed by the named <-for-<= mutation, and the row's justification checks out -- CheckpointWriterContentTest.java:123-124 commits 9 then 4, strictly lower, so the existing fixture cannot see the exact-equal case that IS the retry. A no-op dedup that records, checkpoints, recovers and never consults is named explicitly. Vacuity of the checkpoint inversion is closed by the 'seeding the pods map at write time makes containsEntry green while the replay still commits twice' bullet, and I confirmed the RED claim by reading the fixture: with the fold, the successor's pods map becomes {poda=42, podb=0} and doesNotContainKey("poda") at line 156 fails as claimed, with no K change. The one mutation I could construct that survives every named assertion -- dedup keyed on the segment key STRING rather than on (podId, flushSeq) -- is not a defect: it refuses the retry, accepts the restart, and is one of the mechanisms M4.10b is explicitly free to choose. That the assertions are mechanism-independent in exactly that way is what makes the decomposition sound, and it is the opposite of the failure recorded for rounds 4 and 5.
tier_and_standards: No tier finding. Everything M4.10d prescribes sits at T0 against RecordingBinStore over MemoryBinStore with an injected frozen clock -- no socket, no wall clock, no system temp, no fixed port, fake over mock. Non-negotiable 8 is respected structurally: M4.10c is carved out precisely so a format change lands atomically with its ADR, goldens, readers, writers and fakes rather than as a hunk. Non-negotiable 2 is respected: the tripwire is inverted, never deleted, and the row says so in the language of testing.md rule 5. No existing assertion is weakened by this diff, which stages only three documentation files.
